summary: Auto-wah with five filters (two- and four-pole low-passes and peaks) and nine LFO shapes sweeping the cutoff, with depth, rate, a settable phase and a cutoff inertia. Mono. For more varied wah sweeps than WahMan.
use_for: Auto-wah with a choice of filter types and LFO shapes for more varied sweeps.
quirks: Mono, one track: NeoBuzz Live feeds it left + right summed. Hot: +10 dB at its defaults, +4.3 dBFS peak; Resonance at its top is +12.5 dBFS.
Cutoff is 264 Hz x 32^(v/240) (264 Hz to 8.4 kHz, a step 1/48 octave); LFO depth is in those steps, plus or minus half the value.

Its own default for Set LFO phase (255) is out of range and NeoBuzz Live takes 127; this build starts the LFO phase and the cutoff glide at 0, where upstream's started wherever its memory happened to hold.
The Theviderness factor attribute (0 by default) scales resonance down at low cutoffs.

track_parameters.name: Cutoff
track_parameters.description: Cutoff before the LFO: 264 Hz x 32^(v/240), 264 Hz to 8.4 kHz; a step is 1/48 of an octave (a bare 0 to 240 scale in the manifest).
track_parameters.how: Sets the filter's cutoff before the LFO: 264 Hz x 32^(v/240), 264 Hz to 8.4 kHz in 240 steps.
track_parameters.sound: Low values give a dark, muffled sound; high values open it up. The LFO swings around this point.

track_parameters.name: Resonance
track_parameters.how: Sets the filter's resonance on a 0 to 240 scale (a Q from about 1 to 6); A machine attribute, Theviderness factor (0 by default), can scale resonance down at low cutoffs; at 0 it does nothing.
track_parameters.sound: More resonance gives a sharper, more vocal peak at the cutoff; too much rings and gets loud.

track_parameters.name: Filter
track_parameters.how: Chooses the filter: a two-pole low-pass, two kinds of two-pole peak, a four-pole low-pass or a four-pole peak.
track_parameters.sound: The low-passes cut the top and wah around the cutoff; the peak filters boost around it and sound more vocal.

track_parameters.name: LFO rate
track_parameters.how: Sets the LFO speed from 0.05 Hz to about 27 Hz in an exponential scale.
track_parameters.sound: Slow rates give a long filter breathing; fast ones turn the sweep into a tremolo-like warble.

track_parameters.name: LFO mod
track_parameters.how: Sets how far the LFO moves the cutoff: it swings plus or minus half this many steps, each step 1/48 of an octave, so 240 is plus or minus 2.5 octaves.
track_parameters.sound: Low values give a gentle wobble; high values give a wide, obvious wah sweep. At 0 the cutoff stays where Cutoff puts it.

track_parameters.name: LFO Shape
track_parameters.how: Chooses the LFO wave: sine, rising or falling saw, square, triangle or one of four odd blends of sines.
track_parameters.sound: A sine sweeps smoothly, a saw sweeps then snaps back, a square jumps between two cutoffs, and the random shapes give an unpredictable wobble.

track_parameters.name: Inertia
track_parameters.how: Sets how slowly the cutoff chases its target, 0 to 60: higher values glide more slowly (a step of 10 x e^(-9 v / 240) cutoff steps per 64 samples).
track_parameters.sound: Low values follow the LFO exactly; high values round off the sweep and smooth out jumps from a pattern change.

track_parameters.name: Set phase
track_parameters.description: Set LFO phase. Declared default 255 is outside its range; NeoBuzz Live takes 127
track_parameters.how: Writing a value sets the LFO's position in its cycle: 2 pi x v / 128, 0 to 357 degrees (255 means not written).
track_parameters.sound: Use it to start the sweep from the same place on every bar.
